_source: Git-tracked fallback for curia-suggestion-review's 'genuinely uncertain, ask a human' path. Added 2026-09-04, at explicit user request, after diagnosing the real reason Curia Command's live db (the intended destination — see that tab's own 'How an agent flags something uncertain here' panel) was staying empty: writing to the Artifact tool's db from this job's actual execution environment (a headless RemoteTrigger cloud session) triggers an interactive permission prompt ('Claude wants to edit this artifact's data') that nobody is present to answer — confirmed directly from a real run's session log (get_run_log on session_01KQaCpzGQfZsQASZNnSfDWK, 2026-09-04), not guessed. Reading Curia Command's db works fine unattended (read_db never prompts); only writes are blocked. Git writes (this file) already work perfectly reliably for this job — every venue/district promotion has always gone through git — so uncertain items land here instead, and get synced into Curia Command's real Pending Review tab by a human (or an interactive Claude Code session, which doesn't hit the same wall) during a normal check-in. Once synced, an entry's `syncedToPortal` flips to true; the agent should skip re-syncing (but still re-check `status`) on later runs.

items.reason: Two independent listing sites (Tripadvisor and HappyCow) both explicitly mark King Street Kitchen as CLOSED, and a local Facebook group post laments its closing.
items.researchNotes: Web search 2026-09-05: Tripadvisor's own listing title reads 'King Street Kitchen Knutsford - CLOSED' and HappyCow's review page is headed 'CLOSED: King Street Kitchen - Knutsford Restaurant'. A Facebook group post ('Sad to see King Street Kitchen close, need to make sure...') corroborates. Could not independently confirm an exact closure date or find a same-site successor business. The venue's own Instagram/Facebook pages were not conclusively checked for a contradicting recent 'still open' post, so this is flagged for a human glance rather than auto-removed, per the closure-audit rule. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session (not synced through Curia Command — applied straight to venues.json, same effect).

items.researchNotes: Web search 2026-09-05, following up on the open flag left in docs/data/venues.json's own _dietaryPetSource note (2026-09-04: 'recent reviews suggest it closed a few weeks ago', not acted on at the time). A Tripadvisor review of Riva Bar & Restaurant, 4 Cecil Road, Hale describes turning up to a closed restaurant. Other listings (the venue's own site rivahale.uk, OpenTable-style aggregators) still show it as a going concern with normal weekly closed days (Mon/Tue), so the signal is real but not unanimous — exactly the kind of borderline case this queue exists for rather than an auto-removal. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session (not synced through Curia Command — applied straight to venues.json, same effect).

items.researchNotes: Web search 2026-09-05, following up on the open flag left in docs/data/venues.json's own _dietaryPetSource note (2026-09-04: 'one source... describes its cafe/shop as having closed at some point', not acted on at the time). alderleyedge.com's own article confirms the Front Yard's organic bakery, artisan butchers and greengrocers — the exact 'market-hall energy' this venue's reason text is built on — closed as a cafe/shop; the Back Yard creative/events space may continue separately, so this reads as the venue's real character changing rather than the whole site vanishing, still a call for a human rather than an auto-removal. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session (not synced through Curia Command — applied straight to venues.json, same effect).

items.reason: Only 2 confirmed sites today (Tarporley + Alderley Edge), within the small-sibling-group allowance, but the parent operator publicly states intent to grow this exact brand across Cheshire and the wider North West — the one candidate in today's batch most likely to tip into chain territory soon, so it's a judgment call rather than a clean pass or fail.
items.researchNotes: Independently re-verified 2026-09-06: Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — confirmed real, currently trading, non-chain by site count alone (its own site, firestationsocial.co.uk/locations/, lists exactly two locations: Tarporley and Alderley Edge; no third site found anywhere). However, the parent, Cheshire Pub Company (via its 'Project Social Cucina Ltd' restaurant division), publicly describes itself as actively 'growing their portfolio of individual pubs and inns throughout affluent areas of Cheshire' (cheshirepubco.com/we-are-growing/), and press coverage (thebusinessdesk.com) frames the Alderley Edge opening as 'expansion' with stated ambitions to expand the Fire Station Social Cucina brand across the North West. This is a corporate multi-property operator explicitly building this specific concept toward multi-region rollout, not a single family running two local sites — different in kind from the app's existing 2-3-site sibling-group precedents (Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello), which are all family- or chef-owned pairs with no stated expansion plan. Left pending in docs/data/venue-suggestions.json rather than rejected, since today it still technically passes the site-count bar. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session (not synced through Curia Command — applied straight to venues.json, same effect).

payload.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
payload.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.

items.reason: Les Deux Pizza Bar's own Deliveroo listing currently reads as closed/inactive, and no reopening or 'still trading' signal was found to contradict it.
items.researchNotes: Web search 2026-09-08, routine closure-audit rotating slice (indices 121-125 of docs/data/venues.json): Les Deux Pizza Bar (Alderley Edge) shows as closed on its own Deliveroo page. Older opening coverage (Manchester's Finest, ilovemanchester) is still findable but predates this signal and doesn't confirm current trading. Tripadvisor/food-hygiene/Facebook pages still exist, but that's expected for a recently-closed venue too, not proof it's still open. Not corroborated by a second independent source, so flagged for a human glance per the closure-audit rule rather than auto-removed. The other four venues in this run's slice (The Blind Pig, InHale Yoga, Lions Den, Australasia) all re-confirmed still trading with no closure signal. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session (not synced through Curia Command — applied straight to venues.json, same effect).

items.reason: CAMRA and whatpub.com both list Prana as 'Closed Long Term' since a 28/05/2024 update, but a new company (PRANA F&B LIMITED) was incorporated at the same address four months later and remains active today, and a Food Hygiene Ratings record exists for the venue — genuinely conflicting signals about whether it's trading now, not a clean pass or fail.
items.researchNotes: RESOLVED 2026-09-22: independently re-verified and confirmed permanently/indefinitely closed. Google Maps marks it 'Permanently closed' (posting disabled), its own site returns a dead Cloudflare error, Instagram/Facebook are gone, Skiddle shows zero events ever listed, and its sister venue (Amp, Stockport) also closed and reopened under an unrelated name. The property (14-16 Ashley Road) is listed for sale as former restaurant premises. The Companies House 'Active' status that made this genuinely uncertain in the first pass is a shell company with overdue first accounts, not evidence of an operating business. Not promoted.

payload.name: Prana
payload.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.

items.reason: Companies House shows a cluster of similarly-named entities (a dissolved 'Buon Cibo Cheshire Ltd', a 'Buon Cibo Milano Ltd', and a newly incorporated September 2025 'Buon Cibo Group Ltd' with an active restaurant SIC code) that reads more like an operator scaling up than the simple 2-site family pair this candidate was framed as, and the claimed Reddish sister site couldn't be independently confirmed at all.
items.researchNotes: RESOLVED 2026-09-22: independently re-verified. The flagged Companies House 'expansion cluster' traces to one family (the Ibrahims) — sole director of both the original trading company and the new holding company — folding a messy multi-year company history (repeated compulsory strike-off notices for late filing, not growth) into one entity in Sept 2025. Two real sites confirmed (Hazel Grove takeaway since 2017-19, Heaton Moor sit-down restaurant), no press, franchise language or multi-site hiring found. A genuine small family operation. Promoted (docs/data/venues.json, migration 0038).

payload.name: Buon Cibo
payload.reason: A family kitchen on Shaw Road doing proper Italian without the tablecloth theatre.

items.reason: Genuinely independent and non-chain, but its recent history is a closure announced 17 September 2025, a partial (initially daytime-only) reopening 15 October 2025 after community support, and its original operating company dissolved 12 November 2025 — unclear whether it's trading today, and whether the evening/live-music programme central to its 'Irish bar' identity has come back.
items.researchNotes: RESOLVED 2026-09-22: independently re-verified. Confirmed trading today, but as a daytime-only brunch café-bar (Wed-Sun 9am-4pm) — the evening/live-music Irish-bar identity in the original candidate copy has not visibly returned in the ~11 months since its Oct 2025 reopening (Google/Instagram both show this as the stable steady state). Ownership has a new wrinkle: the original operating company (RUSTIK LTD, the Ahmeds) dissolved Nov 2025; a new same-named company incorporated Jul 2026 under three different directors — flagged honestly rather than carrying over the 'family-run, the Ahmeds' framing uncritically. Promoted with corrected copy/bands/real opening hours (docs/data/venues.json, migration 0038) — not the original 'brunch by day, a proper session by night' framing.

payload.name: Rustik
payload.reason: Burton Road's own Irish corner — brunch by day, a proper session by night, family-run without a single chain tell in the fit-out.

items.reason: A new candidate named 'Underbank' (no 'The') appears to describe the same real venue as this file's own already-promoted 'The Underbank' entry (added 2026-09-11) — the existing entry's reason text (former bank, Des and Nina O'Malley, Pomona Island/Runaway on tap, a basement sound system) matches this candidate fact for fact, while a separate, genuinely different venue on the same street (Benji Taylor's Syndikat-building live-music venue) appears to be the real 'The Underbank' and has apparently never been seeded. This is a naming/identity mix-up between two real venues, not a clean duplicate or a clean distinct-venue case, so it needs a human call rather than a guess.
items.researchNotes: RESOLVED 2026-09-22: independently re-verified. Found no evidence the suspected second venue (Benji Taylor's Syndikat-building 'The Underbank') exists today — the theory traced to a January 2025 Instagram announcement of his plan, which appears to have been superseded by what actually opened in May 2025 (the O'Malleys' 'The Underbank', same building, which itself runs gigs/comedy/quiz nights alongside its beer-hall concept — not purely the narrow 'beer hall' the existing catalog description implies, worth a copy update separately). The existing catalog entry's name is correct as-is; no rename or second entry needed. Not promoted as a new venue.

payload.name: Underbank
payload.reason: A former bank branch turned beer hall and soundsystem room at the crossroads of the two Underbanks — Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, and a rig loud enough that conversation moves to the beer garden after ten.

items.reason: Founder died in 2018, and the only post-2018 source found says the space was slated to become a pay-to-hire artist space rather than a curated gallery; no 2024-2026 source confirms current status either way.
items.researchNotes: Checked artbiogs.co.uk, northernsoul.me.uk, sulisfineart.com, theskinny.co.uk (lists it, undated). All coverage is from 2018 or earlier. No confirmation of current trading status, hours, or curated-vs-rental-space model today. Future pass should check directly before re-suggesting.

items.researchNotes: Repeated the search: same syndicated directory listing found, near-identical wording across both research passes (one source in substance), zero customer reviews on Google/Tripadvisor/Facebook. No closure signal either. Worth a live phone/site check before promoting.

items.reason: Blossom Street Social (51 Blossom Street, Ancoats) closed in June 2026 after nearly 7 years; the site has been trading since July 2026 as a new venue, Mielle (Japanese-inspired café/patisserie/bar run by Paul Chan and his wife) — confirmed independently via CAMRA's venue history record and corroborating local coverage, not just the two research notes that originally flagged it.
items.researchNotes: Sources checked: (1) CAMRA listing for Mielle, Ancoats (camra.org.uk/pubs/mielle-ancoats-199157) - states 51 Blossom Street was occupied by Blossom Street Social 2019-June 2026, now Mielle since July 2026. (2) Britbrief 'Blossom Street Social in Ancoats Closes After Nearly Seven Years' - closure announced via venue's own Instagram. (3) Britbrief 'Mielle Patisserie: Japanese-Inspired Cafe and Bar Opens in Ancoats' - names Paul Chan and wife as owners, opened ~11 July 2026. (4) Confidentials/Taste of Manchester/Manchester Wire - independently confirm Blossom Street Social's original identity and address, ruling out an address mix-up. All sources agree on the same address, timeline and succession; no source suggests Blossom Street Social is still trading. Mielle itself has already been promoted into venues.json by this same run.
